html:
A revolt of Britons against Roman rule around 60 to 61 CE, led by Boudica, queen of the Iceni of what is now Norfolk.

Her husband Prasutagus, a king allied to Rome, left half his kingdom to the emperor Nero and half to his daughters, hoping to protect them. Instead Roman officials seized everything. Boudica was flogged and her daughters raped. The Iceni rose, and the Trinovantes, angry at Roman veterans who had taken their land, joined them.

The governor Suetonius Paulinus was far away, attacking the druids on the island of Anglesey. The rebels burned three towns: Camulodunum (Colchester), Londinium (London) and Verulamium (St Albans). Tacitus says some 70,000 people were killed. Burned layers from that fire still show up in digs in London.

Paulinus gathered a much smaller army, chose his ground well, and crushed the rebels somewhere in the Midlands. Boudica died soon after, by poison or illness. Nero is said to have thought about leaving Britain. In the end Roman rule stayed, with gentler governors (see Claudius invades Britain).
sum: A revolt of Britons against Roman rule around 60 to 61 CE, led by Boudica, queen of the Iceni of what is now Norfolk.
